rubric: Child-safety and age-level tagging of every Sheikh quotation, per the director's instruction to exclude any kids-unsuitable or unsafe text for all of Levels 1-4 regardless of authenticity. An item gets levels [] (excluded for all children) if it contains killing, fighting, war or battle context, blood, slaughter, punishments, torture, graphic Hell/grave/Judgement fear imagery or a warning of Hell, curses, the womb/embryo, marriage/wives/sexual matters, slavery, death as the subject, satan/jinn fear, anything that could frighten, shame or confuse a child, a harsh or threatening tone, sectarian or theologically contentious content, Sufi-technical content, detailed fiqh rulings, archaic wording a child would misread as harsh or rude, or text that starts/ends mid-sentence or carries placeholders; when in doubt it is excluded. Otherwise: Level 1 (ages 4-6, read aloud) only very short (about 25 words or fewer after the narrator chain), concrete, warm, one idea; Level 2 (ages 7-8) up to about 45 words, a simple story or instruction; Level 3 (ages 9-10) up to about 80 words with a clear meaning; Level 4 (ages 10-14) may be longer and abstract (intention, sincerity, self-examination) and is the only level for archaic English (al-Ghazali tr. Claud Field, Pickthall) and for long isnad-heavy hadith texts. Ibn Kathir seerah passages are allowed only where the history is calm (no battles, deaths or attacks); the Year of the Elephant campaign, persecution/torture, Badr/Uhud/Trench and the Prophet's death are excluded. Traits list the counselling situations (nervous, discouraged, comparing, proud, bored, angry, sad, guilty, unkind, lazy, grateful) that the text directly speaks to; excluded items carry no traits. 'why' is given whenever an item is excluded or misses a level.
